text: An ADVENT Security Tower is a fixed rotating structure emitting red light that can be found on many maps; approaching too close (moving into its detection radius or crossing it by diagonal movement) to a security tower will break concealment.

The Encrypted Codex Data is a research project in XCOM 2. It can be researched in the Shadow Chamber after completing the Codex Brain research in the Shadow Chamber. After completing the research a player will be tasked to 'Use the Skulljack on a Codex'.

The Avenger Defense is a unique optional mission in XCOM 2s campaign. A failed mission will end the game. It is very likely to appear at least once in a campaign, as the storyline path summons a UFO after the completion of either one of the story missions. It can only be skipped by completing the game before the UFO hits.

Alien Rulers are new enemies added to XCOM 2 through the Alien Hunters DLC. The three Alien Rulers introduced in the DLC are: the Viper King, the Berserker Queen, and the Archon King. The player cannot encounter multiple rulers in the same mission. The first to appear is the Viper King, then the Berserker Queen and the last is the Archon King. The next ruler typically won't appear until the previous one is killed or successfully escaped.

Retaliation is one of the two ADVENT methods of combating the Resistance in XCOM 2. As opposed to the more esoteric AVATAR Project, Retaliation consists of the more tried-and-true method of stamping down the boot heel until the opponent stops moving.

The Bolt Caster is a primary weapon introduced in XCOM 2's Alien Hunters DLC. The prerequisite project - Experimental Weapons - is available when the "Integrated Downloadable Content" option is enabled in War of the Chosen. If the option is disabled and the Alien Hunters DLC is enabled, then all weapons and items which are unlocked by the research will be found after scanning at Locator Beacon.
The Archon King Autopsy is a research project with Alien Hunters DLC.
The Berserker Queen Autopsy is a research project with Alien Hunters DLC.
A Berserker Queen Corpse is the corpse of the Berserker Queen in the XCOM 2 DLC Alien Hunters.
An Archon King Corpse is the corpse of the Archon King in the XCOM 2 DLC Alien Hunters.

Chryssalid Poison is a status effect in XCOM 2. It can be inflicted on any biological target that isn't immune to Poisoned by the melee attack of a Chryssalid. It doesn't function like the Poisoned status effect, inflicting no penalties, but it does more damage (1-3). Just like regular poison, it can be cured by using a medikit, medical protocol, or extracting. Chryssalid Poison lasts indefinitely until it is cured or the poison kills the unit. Upon being killed, the unit's corpse becomes A Chryssalid Cocoon. Therefore, it is highly recommended to cure Chryssalid Poison whenever it is inflicted on one of your soldiers.

The ADVENT Purifier is an ADVENT enemy encountered in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. They serve as ADVENT's Lost cleanup squads in old world cities, but are also used as incendiary specialists in the fight against XCOM . In combat, ADVENT Purifiers somewhat resemble Grenadier type infantry, but bear one striking difference - rather than a Mag Cannon, their primary weapon is an ADVENT Flamethrower. However, likely because of alien technology, said Flamethrower has much greater range than it appears. As for the unit itself, it's heavyset appearance does not hinder it's speed, which allows the unit to reach close to medium range and open fire on enemies (literally). Avenger Assault is a mission only available in the War of the Chosen expansion. It is similar to the base game Avenger Defense as you have to defend the avenger, and failure of this mission will result in an immediate loss of the campaign.
Wotc-priest.jpg Priest1.PNG The ADVENT Priest is an ADVENT enemy encountered in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. They serve as Psionic support specialists for both ADVENT and Aliens.

The Autopistol is a secondary weapon used by the Templars in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen. It is the conventional pistol that the Templars use, identical to the Pistol. However, it is aesthetically different in that it fires several bullets per shot instead of single-shot action.

Breakthroughs and Inspirations are special Research Projects available in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. Whenever a Research Project is completed, there is a chance you may be offered a single breakthrough or inspiration, at random; you must research it immediately, or the opportunity will expire, unless: # If you also have one or more "Instant" research projects available, you can research the instant options first, and the opportunity will not expire. # If you opt to pursue Shadow Chamber project(s) instead, the opportunity will not expire. Thus, you can safely defer breakthrough/inspiration research in favor of unlocking Avatar project objectives.
The Darkclaw is a unique secondary weapon exclusive to the XCOM 2: War of the Chosen for XCOM 2. It is a futuristic looking, revolver style pistol.

The Arashi is a primary weapon in the War of the Chosen expansion for XCOM 2. It is the Chosen Assassin's secondary weapon. The Arashi comes equipped with four superior weapon upgrades, one more than can be on XCOM's weapons. It also has slightly higher critical damage over the Storm Gun.
The ADVENT Priest Autopsy is a research project in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
The Disruptor Rifle is the signature weapon of the Chosen Warlock in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
Bonding is a new feature introduced in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
Assassin Weapons is a research project in the XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
Experimental Weapons is a research project in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen, with integrated DLC turned enabled.

Covert Actions (or Covert Operations) allow XCOM to raise their level of Influence with each Resistance Faction and are a task necessary to defeat The Chosen. Raising faction Influence involves completing 3 consecutive 'Hunt the Chosen' operations for each of the designated parties, and is required in order for their bases of operations to become objectives available for assault. Until they are eliminated, they will remain possible obstacles on all missions within their established regions, but defeating them is not a requirement of game completion (see: Avatar Project). With each consecutive level of Influence, XCOM will be permitted to employ an additional Resistance Order associated with
The ADVENT General is an ADVENT enemy encountered in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. They assume the role of ADVENT leader in the Neutralize Field Commander mission type.

Explosive Objects are cover objects that can be shot to cause damage to them. Once the hp reaches 0, they explode They can be shot by anyone, or can explode after a hit by grenades or an environmental fire.
The Elerium Phase cannon is the highest tier weapon for the SPARK in the Shen's Last Gift DLC.
An ADVENT Priest Corpse is a corpse of an ADVENT Priest in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.
An ADVENT Purifier Corpse is a corpse of an ADVENT Purifier in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen.

The ADVENT Network Tower Assault is the penultimate storyline mission of XCOM 2. It is unlocked immediately after completing the Avatar Autopsy Shadow Project. This mission carries a randomized designation and is only available once per campaign. The aim of the mission is to hack the global ADVENT network tower, seize control, and broadcast the message of the Resistance to the world. There are no rewards after this mission.

Central's Archives is a major new game mode in the XCOM 2: War of the Chosen – Tactical Legacy Pack DLC for XCOM 2. It consists of four series of pre-defined missions, taking place between the events of XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2: * Blast from the Past – After the fall of XCOM HQ, Central Officer Bradford begins his journey to build the resistance by returning to where it all began. * It Came from the Sea – The broadcast of a fledgling radio DJ is reaching an audience he didn’t intend. A Cease Fire Grenade is a Utility Item in XCOM: Chimera Squad.
Crew Chief Yarvo and Custodian Xel are the main dual leadership for the criminal faction Gray Phoenix in XCOM: Chimera Squad.
An Adhesion Grenade is a Utility Item in XCOM: Chimera Squad.
Celestial Gauntlets are the third tier of Gauntlet weapons available to Templars.

An autopsy is a procedure performed after death for the purposes of research. It is XCOM's primary method of understanding the alien threat. These are categorized by game: * Enemy Unknown * XCOM 2
The Elders are the main antagonists of XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2, controlling ADVENT and responsible for the Avatar Project.

Base visits are intermissions in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified, where Agent Carter visits the Bureau headquarters to advance the plot, plan dispatches, and otherwise interact with other Bureau members. The first visit takes place on the morning of October 29, 1962.

Headquarters of the Bureau of Operations and Command, also just XCOM Headquarters are the heart of XCOM's ancestor, the aforementioned Bureau. Located in San Felipe, California, the vast underground base has taken on an unlikely role during the Zudjari Invasion.

Dodge is a stat in XCOM 2. "An increased Dodge stat can lead to "graze" shots, where only partial damage is applied." *Each point of Dodge stat represents a percent chance for a unit to take reduced damaged from shots and melee attacks. *The damage is halved and rounded down first without taking Armor points into account, which then can potentially nullify the damage. *The damage reduced by Dodge cannot be less than 1, however, the Armor can absorb it. *Dodge can only be triggered by attacks which do not have 100%+ Aim accuracy, and Dodge is not activated by AOE attacks such as grenades. *Dodge cannot be activated if a unit is attacked with Katana or Bolt Caster. Some enemy units have Dodge.

Units in XCOM 2 can use all two action points per turn to move further. Some players call dashing yellow walking. If before dashing Run and Gun was used the unit can shoot a target after dashing. Slash might also activate the 0.7 aim penalty for enemies on overwatch.

The Commander's Avatar is an Avatar in XCOM 2 deployed as an XCOM soldier in the final mission of the campaign, Alien Fortress Assault. The Commander's Avatar is constructed by Chief Science Officer Richard Tygan after completion of the Avatar Autopsy Shadow Chamber research project. Tygan creates the Commander's Avatar by combining the genetic blueprint from the recovered Avatar Corpse with the Avatar template recovered by analyzing the Stasis Suit from the ADVENT Forge Facility and the vial of genetic material recovered from the ADVENT black site. Bleeding is a status effect in the XCOM 2: War of the Chosen DLC.

The EVAC zone is a designated area on an XCOM 2 mission map where deployed soldiers can evacuate from a marked 3 by 3 square to the Skyranger. Once soldiers move into the EVAC zone, they can rope out to the Skyranger and exit the mission without spending an action point. In most missions, XCOM can place an EVAC zone anywhere on the map. However, in Council Missions, Ambushes, the ADVENT Blacksite Assault, and the ADVENT Forge Facility Assault, a fixed EVAC zone is provided. Council Missions, Ambushes, and Alien Facility Assaults are completed by using EVAC zones to extract the deployed squad, as are the key missions ADVENT Blacksite Assault and ADVENT Forge Facility Assault. The Chosen did not appear on Challenge Mode missions and XCOM soldiers were not available as enemy units due to AI issues. Missions represent XCOM ground combat operations and are the key tactical gameplay element in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. During missions the player directs a squad of soldiers in tense turn-based combat, exploring maps shrouded by the "fog of war" to engage the alien ground forces and locate objectives. Most missions are launched from Mission Control via the Geoscape with the exception of Council Missions which are launched from the Situation Room.

The Heavy Class is a soldier class in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The primary role of the Heavy Class is delivering large-scale damage to as many targets as possible, through the use of explosive ordinance or heavy gunfire. It is the only soldier class capable of using rocket launchers, which provide high area damage and demolish obstacles.

The Gray Market is accessible through the Situation Room for XCOM: Enemy Unknown added in XCOM: Enemy Within. Here the Commander can sell recovered alien artifacts and materials to the Council members at any time. The market is essential for raising quick cash when needed, but keep in mind that some research projects, Foundry projects, and many of the items produced in Engineering can require alien materials or corpses.

The Large Scout is an alien spacecraft in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Despite their small size, these reconnaissance craft are not particularly fast, and even Raven Interceptors should get a decent amount of time on target -- enough to bring it down with Avalanche Missiles. Bradford's introduction: "Commander, we've got another contact. The signature is a little bigger this time though."
Research Credits are obtained by interrogating live aliens. Each credit reduces the time required to complete associated Foundry and research projects by 50%.
Guided Fusion Launcher is a research project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

Research projects are the primary way in which new technology, equipment and facilities are unlocked in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Research projects vary from the study, reverse-engineering, and application of recovered alien technologies to performing autopsies on alien corpses and even to the interrogation of captured alien specimens. The completion of research is the primary function of scientists and the more scientists you have the quicker research projects finish; research credits also significantly reduce the amount of time required for specific research projects. The Firestorm is an advanced type of Interceptor used by XCOM in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The Firestorm is the product of the reverse-engineering of many of the aliens' UFO technologies and integrating them into a hybrid fighter craft.

Mission Control is one of the static facilities in the XCOM Headquarters in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Accessing this room provides the player with use of the hologlobe and a list of Upcoming Events. This facility is run by Central Officer Bradford.
As XCOM: Enemy Unknown is based on Unreal Engine 3, it is possible to for users to mod PC versions of the game, allowing for a player to tweak (or cheat) the campaign to their liking.

The Multiplayer game mode allows you to play XCOM: Enemy Unknown online, pitting your tactical prowess against random people or amongst friends. You are able to design a squad of up to six units and play on one of several maps turn by turn against your foe.
Hardened is a trait of numerous units that cannot take cover in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
Improved Arc Thrower is a Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
The Lieutenant rank is the fourth rank available to soldiers. Having a soldier at this rank unlocks Rapid Recovery for purchase at the Officer Training School.

Ironman is a game mode in XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2 that disables manual saving. When Ironman mode is enabled, the campaign's progress is stored on one auto-saving game file, with the option to save multiple game files disabled. Ironman makes the game significantly more difficult as it enforces permadeath for soldiers and forces players to deal with the consequences of mistakes and bad luck. Ironman replaces the standard "Save Game" and "Load Game" options with a "Save and Quit" option that returns the player to the main menu. The Overseer Crash Site is an essential mission in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. This mission carries a randomized Operation designation. The Overseer Crash Site mission plays similarly to a UFO Crash Site mission involving a Large Scout, but with several unique elements.

Items are available to soldiers in XCOM: Enemy Unknown via an additional equipment slot that supplements the weapon and body armor slots. Items fulfill a variety of functions from boosting armor HP to specialty roles like healing. An Outsider Elite is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. The Outsider Elite is a Zudjari with heavy armor and a shield and is commonly seen with other Outsiders. The Outsider Elite uses suppressing fire and grenades to keep your squad off balance, but isn't afraid to close the distance as they can release a stunning melee attack.
The Laser Pulse Rifle is a weapon in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
The Recon Class is one of the Agent types in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
Invasion! is the initial mission in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. This mission serves as a tutorial and prologue to the game; it takes place on 28 Oct, 1962 at the Groom Range facility.
Mosaic is the name given to a vast communication network that allows Origin to assert dominion over his entire empire in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
The Heavy Plasma Pistol is a weapon in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.
The Infiltrator is a Zudjari enemy and brief ally encountered in the XCOM headquarters during the beginning campaign missions of The Bureau: XCOM Declassified.

A MEC or Mechanized Exoskeletal Cybersuit (aka MEC Suit) is a specialized combat rig utilized by a MEC Trooper in XCOM: Enemy Within. Their technology forms the basis of ADVENT MECs in XCOM 2.

Plasma Weapons are advanced weapons manufactured by alien invaders and later by human paramilitary organizations actively engaged in counter-extraterrestrial warfare in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

The Overseer is a unique alien spaceship in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Hidden by special cloaking technology, the Overseer only becomes detectable after building the Hyperwave Relay. Once the Hyperwave Relay is activated, the Overseer will be spotted over a randomized country with satellite coverage and XCOM will be granted the chance to intercept the UFO. The Overseer is the fastest alien ship encountered in the game and more durable than the identically sized Large Scout. It is the only alien craft fitted with dual armaments. In addition to the Plasma II weapon (see infobox), it also has a Plasma I (300 damage, 0 armor penetration at all game difficulties). These weapons fire independently of on

This is an alternate guide for Impossible Ironman difficulty as the other guides were originally written prior to the release of XCOM: Enemy Within. It complements the other guides and has spoilers, but no one should be playing Impossible/Ironman on their first playthrough. The first few months of the game are the most difficult, and it may take a few attempts to get through the first month in decent shape. After that it is manageable every time if played right. Even so, bad things will happen and damage must be kept to a minimum. Soldiers will die: make peace with it.

Operation Progeny is a set of linked Council Missions included in XCOM: Enemy Within. The missions take place in France and introduce a new playable character, a woman named Annette who joins XCOM as a psionically gifted soldier. Like Operation Slingshot, it can be enabled or disabled separately in the game's start up menu. XCOM will face off against the aliens in all the missions; narratively the missions involve all three factions in XCOM: Enemy Within and even have a tie-in with the XCOM Base Defense mission.

Hangar 6: R&D is a DLC campaign available for The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. It was orginally released on November 8th 2013 as an exclusive XBOX 360 piece of content but has since been made available for purchase and download on PC platforms. The DLC offers an eight mission mini-campaign that serves as the prequel to XCOM Declassified's storyline.
The Ranger Class is a soldier class in XCOM 2; any Rookie soldier can become a Ranger in the Armory once they earn enough XP during missions or Covert Actions.
The Grenadier Class is a soldier class in XCOM 2; any Rookie soldier can become a Grenadier in the Armory once they earn enough XP during missions or Covert Actions.
Gatekeeper.jpg XCOM2_Preview_Gatekeeper_04.jpg XCOM2_Preview_Alien_Gatekeeper_Open_3.jpg The Gatekeeper is an alien enemy encountered in XCOM 2. The Gatekeeper occupies a 2×2 tile area.
The Psi Operative is a soldier class in XCOM 2; once a Psi Lab has been built, any Rookie soldier can undergo training to become a Psi Operative.
A Fusion Blade is a sword in XCOM 2. It has 100% chance to cause burning status effect to the hit targets.

The Magnetic Rifle is a primary weapon in XCOM 2. It is an XCOM-produced variant of the ADVENT magnetic rifles. Once purchased in Engineering, upgrades all Assault Rifles (in unlimited quantity). Resistance soldiers, e.g. in ADVENT Retaliation Missions, will have their assault rifles upgraded as well despite not having any visual changes to their guns and ammo, now dealing 4 (+2 critical) damage instead of 2 (+1 critical) damage by their default Assault Rifles. Note that for the upgrade to take effect for the resistance soldiers' weapons, the Assault Rifle upgrade must be performed before a Retaliation Mission location spawns on the Geoscape.
This page is intended to archive the results of past polls featured on the XCOM Wiki home page.
A GREMLIN is a highly specialized drone in XCOM 2 used by Specialists as a secondary weapon. Default model.

An Incendiary Grenade is an explosive grenade and utility item in XCOM 2. An Incendiary Bomb is an improved version of the Incendiary Grenade and comes with the same effects along with more damage, armor shred, and increased radius.
A Proximity Mine is an explosive grenade and utility item in XCOM 2.
The Resistance Communications is a research project in XCOM 2.
The Gatekeeper Autopsy is a research project in XCOM 2's campaign.
Grapples are part of the Skeleton Suit and Ghost Armor. Grappling was considered a move and used an action point.

Predator Armor is a tier 2 medium armor in XCOM 2. The Predator Armor improves on the standard Kevlar Armor by increasing the health of the wearer, and offers a second utility item slot granting soldiers increased tactical flexibility in their loadouts. It is automatically applied to all XCOM soldiers wearing Kevlar Armor when the upgrade is purchased, and is in infinite quantity.
A GREMLIN Mark II is an advanced GREMLIN drone in XCOM 2. It is used by Specialists as a secondary weapon.
A GREMLIN Mark III is a highly advanced GREMLIN drone in XCOM 2. It is used by Specialists as a secondary weapon.

The Living Quarters is a facility aboard the Avenger in XCOM 2. From this facility the player can access the Personnel list which opens the full roster of all soldiers, engineers, and scientists aboard the Avenger as well as their current status or assignment. XCOM soldiers and other personnel can frequently be seen eating, drinking and relaxing here.
The Psionic Gate is a Shadow Chamber research project in XCOM 2. It must be completed to progress the story.
Radio Relays reduces the Intel cost of nearby regions when making contact. It also increases the amount of supplies of the region it's built on during the monthly supply drop.

Grenades are a class of weapons in XCOM 2. Only the Frag Grenade is available at the start of the game. All other grenades are unlocked via Engineering, Research, Proving Ground projects, or scanning a Convoy Ambush rumor location on the Geoscape.

Intel is a strategic resource in XCOM 2. It is identified as passcodes, coordinates, information that can benefit XCOM in their siege on ADVENT. Research Projects: Alien Data Cache Decryption and ADVENT Datapad Decryption will give 1 time boost. Intel is gained through certain Hack Rewards (Guaranteed to have Intel reward option for Skullmining), completing certain missions types (Guaranteed to have Intel reward for Council missions), and Scanning at the player's home base with the respective scanning bonus active. The Recovered ADVENT Stasis Suit is a Shadow Chamber research project in XCOM 2. It must be completed to progress the story.
Patches are software updates designed to fix bugs and performances issues and/or improve gameplay, game balance or system functionality for XCOM 2.

Panic is a status effect in XCOM 2. Chances to panic from non-psionic attacks are entirely dependent on a unit's Will stat; the higher the Will of a unit, the less likely they are to panic in situations where they would Panic.
The R.A.G.E. Suit and its upgrade, the R.A.G.E. Armor, are heavy armors available in the Alien Hunters DLC for XCOM 2.
The R.A.G.E. Armor, which is the upgrade of the R.A.G.E. Suit, is a heavy armor available in the Alien Hunters DLC for XCOM 2.

The Icarus Armor is medium armor in XCOM 2 available with the Alien Hunters DLC. Only one instance of Icarus Armor can be built per game, and will be permanently lost if the wearer is captured or killed, and their body not evacuated.

The Frost Bomb is a Grenade exclusive to XCOM 2's Alien Hunters DLC. The grenade freezes all targets caught in the blast radius. The prerequisite project - Experimental Weapons - is available when the "Integrated Downloadable Content" option is enabled in War of the Chosen. If the option is disabled and the Alien Hunters DLC is enabled, then all weapons and items which are unlocked by the research will be found after scanning at Locator Beacon.

The Hunter's Axe is a unique secondary weapon introduced in the Alien Hunters DLC for XCOM 2. The prerequisite project - Experimental Weapons - is available when the "Integrated Downloadable Content" option is enabled in War of the Chosen. If the option is disabled and the Alien Hunters DLC is enabled, then all weapons and items which are unlocked by the research will be found after scanning at Locator Beacon.
The Heavy Autocannon is the basic weapon for the SPARK class in XCOM 2.

The Kal-7 Bullpup is a primary weapon introduced in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen. It is the signature conventional weapon of the Skirmishers. Shooting using a Bullpup rifle only costs a single action and does not end the Skirmisher's turn. This allows the Skirmisher to shoot and move in any order, or shoot twice in a single turn.
The Magnetic Bolt Caster is a primary weapon introduced in the XCOM 2 DLC Alien Hunters.
Frozen is a status effect introduced in the Alien Hunters DLC.

Negative Traits are modifiers that can affect soldiers in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. Soldiers randomly may perform undesired actions under conditions that depend on the Negative Trait possessed (see below). Negative Traits can be gained through combat when a soldier is wounded by a certain enemy, fails a certain action enough times, or simply obtains it naturally. Negative Traits that involve taking a specific action can be avoided by taking an action that uses up all the unit's actions (i.e., dashing, firing, Overwatch, etc.). Julian Gollop is a British video game designer and producer specializing in strategy games, who has founded and led Mythos Games, Codo Technologies and Snapshot Games. He is known best as the "man who gave birth to the X-COM franchise."
The Reinforced Underlay is an upgrade in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen that is activated upon the completion of the ADVENT Purifier Autopsy research.

In XCOM 2 Guerilla Ops are a standard series of missions that are aimed at countering ADVENT's Dark Events. In each Guerilla Op, the player controls a squad of elite soldiers with the aim of engaging ADVENT and alien forces to complete mission objectives. Their location is marked by a green ADVENT trooper () on the Geoscape, and they will only spawn on locations you have established contact with. In extremely rare cases, a single Guerilla Op may be spawned through a Rumor. Depending on the expansion, there are up to six Guerilla Ops missions (four in XCOM 2, with two added in War of the Chosen). In XCOM 2 and its expansions, a pod refers to a group of enemies patrolling a certain area. Many of the aliens fall into one of two categories - pod leaders and pod followers. Missions are ranked on their difficulty, which is proportional to the amount of pods that will be patrolling the area during the mission: * Easy - between 2-4 pods * Moderate - between 5-6 pods * Difficult - between 7-8 pods * Very Difficult - between 8-10 pods

The KAL-15 Bullpup is a primary weapon introduced in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen. It is an upgrade of the Skirmishers' signature Kal-7 Bullpup.
Kal-90 Bullpup is a primary weapon introduced in the XCOM 2 expansion, War of the Chosen. It is an upgrade of the Skirmishers' improved Kal-15 Bullpup.
Four concealed rookie soldiers must neutralize all enemy forces and plant an X4 on the Elder monument. If all four soldiers die or get mind controlled, the game ends.

In XCOM 2, the Geoscape is a strategic overview of the Earth accessible from the Bridge of the Avenger. The Geoscape is where the Commander performs the operations of XCOM on Earth. The Commander scans for hostile alien actions, contact resistance cells, seek out valuable resources, and move the Avenger. Dark Events: ADVENT is hard at work on their own plans to topple the resistance; if completed, they provide bonuses to the enemy. Dark events inform you of ADVENT’s progress towards completing their goals. XCOM can counter their progress by choosing certain Guerilla Ops missions.

Hack defense is an attribute in XCOM 2. Note that all ADVENT soldiers have 125 Hack defense regardless of the game difficulty or the enemy unit tier, and the Hack defense comes into play only when an enemy soldier is being Skullmined. Other enemy units and turrets - which can be hacked with Haywire Protocol - have their own Hack defense stat values.

The maps in XCOM 2 are semi-randomly generated. Bits and pieces of the maps are handcrafted and every time randomly put into a different place. The possible atmospheric variables (according to defaultmaps.ini) are: Time of day: noon, dusk, dawn, sunset, night. Weather: clear, rain.

The mobile gacha game XCOM Legends featured 51 recruitable heroes, divided into three classes of rarity: Epic, Rare, and Uncommon. Each hero was classified by faction, role, type, and class. Epic heroes had access to War Stories, personal missions that raised level caps and unlocked biographical lore and personal weapons. The game's data files stored the age of each hero but their ages weren't displayed in-game.

The XCOM Headquarters is the main base of operations for XCOM and the player's primary interface for managing the strategic elements of XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Nicknamed the "ant farm" by the game developers, it is here the player must manage resources, research projects, facilities and various other undertakings throughout the game. The XCOM: Enemy Unknown manual refers to the base and its facilities collectively as the Geoscape view. =Facilities= The XCOM Headquarters is made up of numerous facilities that are responsible for managing and supplementing the base's important strategic and research functions.
The Skyranger is a specialized rotor-craft used by XCOM in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified, and is the forerunner of the later Skyranger craft that saw operation during XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

Rosemont, Georgia is one of the mission locations in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. Agent Carter and his team is sent here to recover a Dr. Alan Weir from the local university. The town was attacked during the middle of a homecoming parade; the streets are littered with abandoned vehicles and mutilated bodies.

The Titan is an enemy in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. The ultimate Zudjari war machine, the appropriately named Titan, is one of the most dangerous enemies the player will face in terms of damage output. It shoots a giant laser and terraforms the immediate area around it. The Titan acts as the game's second boss. It is encountered when Agent Carter is on the hunt for the Phase Plotter.

XCOM: Enemy Unknown is the turn-based action-strategy game developed by Firaxis Games, the same company behind the massively successful Civilization games. The game re-imagines the classic UFO: Enemy Unknown/X-COM: UFO Defense and brings its tense, tactical gameplay to a new generation. XCOM: Enemy Unknown was released on October 9th, 2012 in North America and on October 12th internationally. XCOM: Enemy Unknown blends strategic base management with turn-based combat in unique and addictive gameplay. A Sectopod is an enemy in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. It's a massive bipedal robot with a heavily armored central 'head' that houses several potent weapon systems.

The Council consists of the group of 16 countries that created XCOM and who continue to fund and support the organization. The Council, represented by its mysterious shadowy spokesman, will make regular contact with the Commander (the player) via the Situation Room. The Council has three primary reasons to contact XCOM: #Propose a new Council Mission. #Present a special request from a member nation asking that XCOM supply them with certain items in exchange for a generous reward (Credits, engineers, scientists, or a new, highly ranked soldier). This request will remain available for fulfillment for 20 days. # Deliver the monthly report that evaluates and rewards XCOM's actions.
The Rocket Launcher is a single-shot weapon used by Heavy Class soldiers in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
Satellites are deployed by XCOM to globally monitor alien activity in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
The Uplink Targeting (Aim) is an armament module for Interceptors in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

The Supply Barge is an alien spacecraft in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Supply Barges are large ships ostensibly used by the invaders to land supplies and equipment. Their appearance, like the appearance of Terror Site missions indicates an escalation of the aliens' campaign tempo. Supply Barges can be encountered during an interception, or as a UFO crash or landing site mission. Capable of withstanding incredible punishment, intercepting a barge is difficult. They carry a substantial crew, so regardless of how a barge makes its appearance, assaulting one is a considerable task. The S.H.I.V. (Super Heavy Infantry Vehicle) is a weapons platform in XCOM: Enemy Unknown that can be manufactured in the Engineering Lab. S.H.I.V.s can be deployed as substitutes for human soldiers on missions and require a space in the XCOM HQ barracks.

UFO Crash Site is a mission type in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. This mission type is nearly identical to UFO Landing Sites. Other than the method of acquisition and 18 hours added to the permissible response time, some of the alien ship's crew may not survive the crash, and equipment on board the UFO may be damaged.
A Sectopod Wreck is the corpse of a Sectopod in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
A Thin Man Corpse is the corpse of a Thin Man in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
A Sectoid Commander Corpse is the corpse of a Sectoid Commander in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
A Sectoid Corpse is the corpse of a Sectoid in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.

UFO Landing Site is a mission type in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Other than the method of acquisition and a decreased window of opportunity to respond, this mission type is nearly identical to UFO Crash Sites. All of the alien ship's crew and equipment are intact at the start of the mission.
Temple Ship Assault is the final mission in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. This mission takes place aboard the Temple Ship off the coast of South America and has the official designation of Operation Avenger.
Target Extraction is a type of Council Missions in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
S.H.I.V. Suppression is a Foundry project in XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
